nonLabourLines.description: Stripe integration sandbox/testing fees and PCI scoping review
Legacy Oracle data migration tooling/licensing and DBA consulting

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) are available for this project yet; estimate is based purely on backlog point-sizing and rate card, not on measured team velocity.
1 story point ≈ 6-7 hours of blended effort across the team, adjusted per task type (integration/migration/security tasks weighted higher than CRUD screens).

Backend Developer role (1.5 FTE = ~120 hrs/week capacity) absorbs API, integration, migration and security-heavy tasks; total allocated hours (1960) imply roughly 16-17 weeks of full utilisation, which is tight against the 1.5 FTE capacity and may require schedule extension or temporary contractor support.
Frontend Developer (1.0 FTE, ~40 hrs/week) allocated 1360 hours implies ~34 weeks of solo full-time work; this is the primary schedule constraint given no second FE hire.

QA Engineer (0.6 FTE, ~24 hrs/week) allocated 640 hours implies ~27 weeks; QA is thinly staffed relative to the number of features requiring regression and security testing (auth, payments, RBAC, GDPR).

DevOps Engineer (0.4 FTE, ~16 hrs/week) allocated 340 hours (~21 weeks) covers CI/CD setup, observability and legacy decommission; treated as a part-time specialist rather than continuous full-time presence.

PW-8 (Legacy data migration, 21 points) is assumed to require significant Backend + DevOps effort and dedicated migration tooling spend, not just linear point-to-hour scaling, due to data volume (400k records, 2M invoice lines).
PW-7 (Payment provider integration) assumed to include webhook handling, reconciliation logic and compliance review, driving extra QA and non-labour spend.
Non-labour costs are rough placeholders for tooling, licensing, external audits and infrastructure; actual vendor quotes have not been obtained.
Contingency of ~8% of labour+non-labour subtotal is included given the absence of historical velocity data and the presence of several high-uncertainty items (migration, multi-currency, payments).
Priority breakdown totals are estimated pro-rata based on story points weighted by task complexity, mapped against the labour cost pool; they are indicative, not a strict task-by-task ledger.
input.reasoning: "Total backlog is 24 tasks totalling 203 story points across Urgent/High/Medium/Low priorities. Given the team composition (1.5 Backend, 1.0 Frontend, 0.6 QA, 0.4 DevOps FTE), I converted story points to hours using a blended ~6.5 hrs/point baseline, then adjusted individual tasks upward where they involve integration, compliance or data-migration complexity (PW-7, PW-8, PW-4, PW-9, PW-14, PW-17) and downward for simpler CRUD/UI tasks (PW-6, PW-12, PW-23). Hours were then allocated across roles per task type: backend-heavy for API/integration/migration work, frontend-heavy for UI/UX and design-system work, QA hours scaled to roughly 25-30% of dev effort reflecting the thin 0.6 FTE QA capacity, and DevOps hours concentrated on CI/CD setup (PW-1), observability (PW-22) and decommissioning (PW-24) reflecting the 0.4 FTE capacity. This produced total labour hours of 1960 (Backend), 1360 (Frontend), 640 (QA) and 340 (DevOps), each proportionate to the stated FTE capacity relative to a ~9-month delivery window, while flagging in assumptions that QA and DevOps are thinly staffed relative to the backlog's risk profile (auth, payments, compliance, migration). Non-labour costs were added for third-party audit, migration tooling, infra and Stripe-related compliance review. Priority-based cost breakdown was derived by mapping each task's estimated hours (via its role allocation and rate) back to its priority label and summing. Three delivery scenarios (Optimistic/Most Likely/Pessimistic) were built by scaling the base labour+non-labour total by -15%/base/+20% to reflect estimation uncertainty given the total absence of historical velocity or actuals data for this team."

reductions.description: Descope PW-18 (Admin back-office for support staff, Low priority, 13 pts) to a later phase; support staff can use existing DB tooling short-term.
reductions.effect: Removes ~13 points of Backend+Frontend+QA effort from initial delivery scope.

reductions.description: Defer PW-19 (Usage analytics and reporting, Low, 8 pts) and PW-23 (Contract tests against helpdesk API, Low, 5 pts) to a post-launch backlog.
reductions.effect: Removes two low-priority, non-customer-facing tasks from the funded scope.

reductions.description: Reduce Accessibility pass (PW-15) scope to core customer journeys only rather than all screens, and skip the external WCAG audit initially, relying on internal review.
reductions.effect: Cuts both engineering hours and the $5,000 external audit line; formal certification deferred to a later release.

reductions.description: Use a managed migration/ETL SaaS tool with built-in Oracle connectors instead of custom-built migration scripts for PW-8, reducing Backend and DevOps hours.
reductions.effect: Cuts ~150-200 hours of custom Backend/DevOps migration coding at the cost of a tooling subscription (already reflected in non-labour), net saving on labour.

reductions.description: Delay Multi-currency support (PW-14, Medium, 13 pts) to a follow-up release, launching with single-currency (USD) support only.
reductions.effect: Removes FX-rate integration, settlement logic and associated QA/backend effort from the initial cost base.

reductions.description: Reduce DevOps involvement in Observability (PW-22) to essential payment-path tracing only, deferring full dashboard/alerting suite.
reductions.effect: Cuts roughly half the allocated DevOps hours for this task while retaining critical payment monitoring.
